title: Provider-Concentration Stress Test: Simulating a Single-Provider Outage in a Multi-Agent Workflow

original_idea.body:
# Provider-Concentration Stress Test: Simulating a Single-Provider Outage in a Multi-Agent Workflow

**Problem:** The International AI Safety Report flags cascading failures when systems depend on one provider, but there is little hands-on study of HOW a small multi-agent workflow degrades when its shared backbone model fails or is swapped.

**Direction:** Vary the agent population's homogeneity in a small multi-agent task. Compare a homogeneous version against a heterogeneous version, and measure how task success and error-catching collapse when the shared model is perturbed.

**Why it matters:** A reproducible micro-demonstration of concentration risk and the protective value of backbone diversity.

**Relevant context:** International AI Safety Report 2026 (arXiv:2501.17805); Risk Analysis for Governed Multi-Agent Systems (arXiv:2508.05687); correlated errors (arXiv:2506.07962).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible concentration-risk demonstration but a toy 3-agent micro-demo's link to catastrophic systemic failure is a stretch.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a multi-agent solve-verify-critique loop plus perturbation harness needs solid engineering.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires a working multi-agent system, homogeneous/heterogeneous variants, and degradation measurement - several moving parts.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: External redundancy/monitoring infra with open models; labs underweight concentration-risk demos.

low_compute.reasoning: Several small open models in a loop; single GPU feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Backbone-diversity robustness in multi-agent systems plausibly partly studied; this micro-demo angle open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multi-agent robustness studied; provider-concentration stress demo is a fresh framing.
